### Consciousness reflects name-and-form as self
"An ordinary individual sees a nāma-rūpa, when he reflects, which he
calls 'I' and 'mine'."
"A non-arahant, upon reflection, sees name-and-form, which however he
mistakes to be his self."

### The cinema beam = ordinary consciousness
"Consciousness is as narrow as that beam of light falling on the cinema
screen. That is to say, the specifically prepared consciousness."

---

### The gem is made by attention
"The gem arose out of what earlier appeared as a rubbish heap. It became
the thing for him, and desire was at the root of this phenomenon."
"With the cessation of that concept of a gem as some special thing, a
valuable thing, separate from the rest of the world... the gem ceases
to exist. That itself is the deliverance."

### The perception of impermanence leads to not-self
"Monks, in one who has the perception of impermanence, the perception
of not-self gets established. With the perception of not-self, he
arrives at the destruction of the conceit 'am', which is extinction
here and now."
Analayo parallel: MĀ 57.

### The perception of impermanence exhausts everything
"Monks, the perception of impermanence, when developed and intensively
practised, exhausts all attachments to sensuality, exhausts all
attachments to form, exhausts all attachments to existence, exhausts all
ignorance, exhausts all conceits of an 'am' and eradicates it completely."
Analayo parallel: SĀ 270.

### Mogharaja's void question
"By looking upon the world in which manner can one escape the eye of the
king of death?"
"Look upon the world as void, Mogharaja, being mindful at all times,
uprooting the lingering view of self, get well beyond the range of death."

### Sabbe dhamma nalams abhinivesaya
"Nothing is worth clinging on to." The word abhinivesa is closely
associated with entering into and getting entangled in views of one's
own creation.

### Latencies from past performances
"Where are the actors and actresses who played their part in the early
acts of our drama of life?... Though they are no more, so long as
latencies to perception, amassed through them, persist in us, there is
nothing to prevent us from indulging in thoughts and proliferations."

### The concept-flush cycle
"In the course of thinking proliferation takes over, with the result
that those concepts throw up a flush that tends to overwhelm and
obsess the one who initiated the whole process."

---

### The truth/falsehood dyad from logic (Cūḷaviyūha)
"There are no several and various truths, that are permanent in the
world, apart from perception. It is by manipulating logic in
speculative views, that they speak of two things called 'truth and
falsehood'."
Analayo parallel: Bodhi (2017: 308).

### Each school calls its own true (Mahāviyūha)
"They call their own system of thought perfect, and the other system
of thought inferior. Thus they quarrel and dispute."
"Sakaṃ sakaṃ sammutim — 'each his own viewpoint'."
Analayo parallel: Bodhi (2017: 310).

### The barb
"He declares that he has seen well in advance 'the barb on which
mankind is hooked impaled'. The barb is none other than the dogmatic
assertion, 'I know, I see, it is verily so'."

---

### The five groups as painted artefacts
"The worldling creates his own form, feelings, perceptions, preparations,
and consciousness — as a painter fashions a likeness on a board."
"Form like foam, feeling like bubble, perception like mirage, volitions
like plantain trunk, consciousness like an illusion."

### Sakkayaditthi = self-bias
"It is such a view that made the dog imagine that there is another dog
in the water. It imagined that the dog is there, even when it is not
looking."

### The winding and rewinding
"The entire world, or samsaric existence in its entirety, is a process
of winding and rewinding. Where the winding ends and the rewinding
begins is a matter beyond our comprehension."
"We go on heaping up karmic actions, but when the time comes to
experience their consequences, we do not regard them as mere results of
karma, but superimpose an 'I' on that experience."
"This is like a tangled skein. Sometimes, when an unskilled person tries
to disentangle a tangled skein while disentangling one end, the other
end gets entangled."

### Dancing as madness
"This, monks, is a form of madness according to the noble one's
discipline, namely dancing. Now what is the nature of a madman? He is
jumpy. From the standpoint of Dhamma, dancing is a form of jumpiness.
In fact, all preparations are that. It shows a nervous stress as well
as a nervous release. It is an endless series of winding and unwinding."
